 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Unai Emery had a big call to make with Ibrahim Mbaye heading into Aston Villa's Carabao Cup clash against Bournemouth on Wednesday. 
 The Villans travel to the Vitality Stadium to face the Cherries in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup, and will be hoping to keep their silverware chances alive.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A Tammy Abraham brace followed by a Ross Barkley finish helped the Villa ease past Coventry City in the previous round, with Emery now keen to add more silverware to the club's trophy cabinet.
 The B6 side can extend their unbeaten run to eight with a win or a draw against Bournemouth, but Marco Rose's side are coming into this one in top form, having one each of their last four games in all competitions without conceding a single goal.
 Emery also has the chance to give some players a well-deserved run out, while still naming a strong side.
 Mbaye has been deserving of a start in recent games, but will he get one against Bournemouth?
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Unai Emery confirms Ibrahim Mbaye decision vs Bournemouth 
 Mbaye has shown promising signs since signing for Villa, having already played eight times for the club.
 He has four assists for the B6 side, but has only started three games under Emery, racking up a total of 323 minutes across all competitions.
 The 18-year-old picked up an assist in a 31-minute cameo in the 2-1 win over Manchester City last weekend, completing 67 per cent of his passes after coming on, setting up Nicolas Jackson for his winning goal.
 The former PSG star earned an 8.1 FotMob rating in his only Carabao Cup appearance after starring in the win over Coventry on 16 September.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Mbaye created the joint-most chances in the match (4) and also had the joint-most touches inside an opposition's box (8).
 Sadio Mane previously called Mbaye an "exceptional player", as per Rousing the Kop , and the Cherries could find out why in this game.
 But will Emery start Mbaye from the off, or bring him on from the bench?
 Well, Villa have confirmed their lineup on X, and Emery has decided to play Mbaye, a decision which will surely pay off in dividends.
 Three Aston Villa questions this week include has Nicolas Jackson made fans forget Ollie Watkins already? Will Villa's away vs Bournemouth give confidence? 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Villa know that they will be in for a tough night at the Vitality.
 The Cherries have beaten Manchester United and AC Milan in their last two matches, winning both games 3-0.
 However, the Villans aren't unfamiliar with success on the south coast.
 Villa have drawn two and won the other of their last three visits to Bournemouth.
 The last time the Villans lost at the Vitality was on 6 August, 2022, when Jefferson Lerma and Kieffer Moore scored the goals for the Cherries.
 Hopefully, if recent history is anything to go by, Villa will be able to get a good result and advance to the next round of the Carabao Cup.
